catalog_description: Tenants, workspaces, or domains of a SaaS platform, tracked as the places where company data resides for security-posture analysis.
Availability and response-time readings for SaaS apps, monitored from multiple locations and networks to capture the experience real users get.
SaaS applications in the company portfolio, with vendor, category, criticality, owner, and whether each is sanctioned or shadow IT.
Contractual subscriptions for SaaS apps: plan tier, seat count, recurring cost, billing cadence, renewal date, and owner.
Per-user activity for each SaaS app: logins, time in app, feature usage, and last-active date, used to right-size licenses.
Workplace injuries, illnesses, near-misses, and unsafe conditions, with investigation, root-cause analysis, and recordability determination.
Pay ranges by grade and geographic zone, with minimum, midpoint, maximum, and benchmark source, guiding offers and pay-equity analysis.
Logged touchpoints between sales and a contact or opportunity: calls, emails, meetings, demos, and content views.
Multi-step outreach sequences defining touchpoints, timing, and branching rules, used to enroll and engage prospects systematically.
Individual one-to-one sales emails sent to prospects, with open, reply, and click tracking and thread context.
Sales-facing content assets such as decks, one-pagers, and demo scripts, managed through draft, publish, and retire states.
Versioned, numbered quote documents with dates, validity, currency, terms, pricing, and status from draft to accepted or lost.
Recoveries of salvageable property or proceeds from damaged or totaled assets after a claim settles, with vendor and recovery amount.
Cleaning and sanitation completion records per shift, line, or piece of equipment, with verification results.
What-if strategic scenarios such as mergers, market disruption, or expansion, used to compare possible futures.
Canonical schemas for data flowing through pipelines, defining field contracts, versions, and evolution rules.
Imported e-learning content packages in standard formats, carrying the content manifest and runtime tracking state.
Safety data sheets for hazardous substances, with hazard classification, exposure limits, and handling guidance for hazard communication.
Shareholder-initiated sales of existing equity: tender offers, employee liquidity programs, or direct transfers, with board approval.
Classes of security in the cap table such as common, preferred series, SAFEs, and warrants, with their rights and preferences.
Audience clusters defined within a digital experience platform for on-site personalization.
Reusable metric and dimension definitions in the semantic layer, governed for consistent use across BI tools and AI agents.
Detected data-security incidents such as over-privilege, exposed sensitive data, or unauthorized access, triggering remediation.
Definitions of what can be requested: the request form, fulfillment workflow, approvals, service level, and charge-back rules.
Planned modifications to a service or configuration item, with change type, risk score, approval state, schedule, and back-out plan.
Meter-to-grid or meter-to-pipe hookup assets, with location, conductor or pipe size, install date, and maintenance history.
Service contracts that carry service-level commitments such as response times, parts coverage, and call-out fees.
Quoted estimates for boatyard work, covering scope, labor hours, parts, and price, approved by the boater before work begins.
Unplanned service interruptions or quality reductions, with severity, priority, category, assignee, and affected components.
Service-level objective definitions and their breach state, with targets, remaining error budget, burn rate, and last breach.
Mappings of named business services to the configuration items that underlie them, linking technical topology to business impact.
Service mesh installations, with traffic policy, mutual-TLS enforcement, and distributed-tracing configuration.
Back-end service definitions covering commitments, supported configurations, and fulfillment, separate from their user-facing catalog items.
Customer-facing outage records, with the affected service, public status, start and end times, and the customer message.
Recurring preventive-maintenance plans for installed equipment, defining cadence, due date, grace window, and overdue escalation.
Root-cause records for recurring or related incidents, with known-error workarounds and links to the fix that will resolve them.
Client-facing engagements with scope, contract, dates, billing type, revenue-recognition method, and assigned project manager.
Orchestration state and task list for activating, changing, or closing a service, showing how a service order is executed.
Release records that bundle one or more changes into a single shippable unit, with the release window, status, and rollback plan.
Planned, catalog-driven requests for access, hardware, software, or information, distinct from reactive incidents.
Service-level agreements setting response, resolution, and availability targets by priority, category, or customer tier.
Subscriber-reported service degradation or outage tickets, with service, severity, timestamps, root cause, and resolution.
Customer-facing service jobs fulfilled by field visits, distinct from preventive-maintenance work orders.
Per-session attendance roster rows for each learner, serving as evidence of completed required workplace training.
Cancellation or no-show records for an instructor-led session, used to drive waitlist promotion.
Video and audit-log artifacts captured from a remote session, with storage location, retention, redaction state, and compliance use.
Pre-session enrollment snapshots for an instructor-led session, used as the basis for attendance proof.
Data stores, files, or SaaS instances found in use but missing from the official inventory: unmanaged or rogue copies.
SaaS apps found in use but not officially sanctioned, discovered through expense data, sign-on logs, browser, or network signals.
Per-shareholder records of holdings across all security classes for an issuer.
Worker requests to swap, give up, or pick up a shift, started on the worker's device and routed for manager approval.
Operator-raised shop-floor issues such as defects, safety concerns, equipment anomalies, or material shortages, for the problem-solving team.
E-signature envelopes with signing audit trail, IP addresses, provider references, and the signed document, one contract may have many.
Connection metadata for downstream data targets: authentication, batch or stream mode, upsert keys, and schema enforcement rules.
Special Investigation Unit fraud cases on insurance claims, with indicators triggered, investigator, status, and any law-enforcement referral.
Proficiency-rating events against a skill, recording the rater, method (self, manager, peer, or test), score, and date.
Peer or manager validations of a claimed skill on a profile: a quick social signal, distinct from a formal assessment.
Audit records of automated skill-inference batches, capturing model version, input signals, outputs, and timestamp.
Per-worker collections of skills with self-assessed and validated proficiency, derived from courses, certifications, and performance signals.
Learning-path steps, each binding a skill to a target proficiency threshold to reach.
Versioned ontologies of skill nodes, with synonyms and parent-child relationships.
Individual skill nodes within a taxonomy version, referenced by every profile entry, competency model, and inference run.
Comparisons of current skills inventory against future demand by role, level, and location, guiding build, buy, or borrow decisions.
Placements of a specific vessel in a specific slip, mooring, or rack for a period, linking inventory to a reservation or contract.
Seasonal or annual agreements licensing a slip, mooring, or rack to a boater, with term, rate, included utilities, and renewal terms.
Requests to dock or store a vessel for a transient or seasonal period, with dates, vessel, requested space, rate, and check-in status.
Configured size classes for slips and racks, defined by length and beam bands, used for fit rules and rate lookup.
Boaters' places in line for a slip type or period that is currently full, with offer and expiry tracking.
System-raised alerts on the SaaS portfolio: shadow-IT signups, projected license overages, opening renewals, or vendor-risk changes.
Per-app utilization and cost-per-seat benchmarks against an industry peer set, snapshotted each measurement period with an outlier flag.
Published listings of sanctioned SaaS apps that employees can browse and request, with description, owner, request route, and approval flow.
Configured connections between the SaaS management platform and an app's APIs for sign-on, provisioning, finance, and usage data.
Portfolio-rationalization stages of a SaaS app such as evaluate, pilot, sanctioned, sunset, and retired.
Typed owner assignments linking a user to a SaaS app as its business, IT, finance, or security owner.
Employee requests for access to a SaaS app via the published catalog, routed for manager and IT approval before provisioning.
Declarative automation workflows with a trigger and steps such as provisioning, notifying, offboarding, or requesting approval.
User-to-app license seat assignments, showing who holds a seat at which tier, its cost, utilization, and last activity, to drive reclamation.
System-generated proposals to right-size or consolidate SaaS spend, with estimated savings, rationale, type, and status.
Executed reclamation actions against a license seat (revoke, downgrade, or reassign), with the savings realized.
Per-renewal-cycle envelopes covering timeline, owner, vendor proposals received, fallback notes, and decisions taken.
Tasks within a SaaS renewal cycle, such as the renewal-window notice, owner assignment, and the renew-or-cancel decision.
Chargeback splits of a SaaS subscription across cost centers, business units, or projects, with the allocation method and effective window.
Quote, counter-quote, and discount records tied to a renewal, documenting how the final commercial terms were reached.
SaaS vendor risk scorecards covering attestation status, data-processing review, subprocessors, breach history, and posture score.
Execution logs for each automation workflow run, with trigger source, input, step-by-step status, output, duration, and any error.
Brand-owned connected accounts on specific social networks, with credentials, permissions, and channel-specific metadata.
Connected advertiser accounts on social ad platforms, under which campaigns are run and billed.
Paid social campaigns defining an advertising objective, schedule, and overall budget, parenting one or more ad sets.
Versioned ad creatives pairing visuals and copy (image, video, carousel), with approval state and platform-specific renditions.
Time-series delivery and outcome metrics per ad, ad set, or campaign, such as impressions, clicks, spend, conversions, and return on ad spend.
Targeting and budget units within a campaign, binding an audience, placements, bid strategy, schedule, and budget to a set of ads.
Individual deliverable ads within an ad set, pairing a creative with destination and tracking and carrying their own delivery state.
Saved monitoring queries defined by keywords, hashtags, competitors, geographies, and sentiment filters that drive social listening.
Brand or keyword mentions detected across networks, news, blogs, forums, and review sites, typically from non-followers off-channel.
Inbound conversations in the unified inbox: comments, direct messages, mention-replies, and reviews on brand-owned accounts.
Authored social posts (draft, scheduled, or published) with per-channel variants, media, copy, lifecycle state, and approval history.
Release events deploying a build to a target environment, with deployer, timestamps, status, rollback flag, and change-ticket reference.
Discovered installs of a software title on a specific device or for a specific user, the operational fact distinct from the licensing right.
